page: Amazon Web Services m7gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro architecture. It features 48 dedicated physical ARMv8 cores using the AWS Neoverse-V1 Graviton processor implementation running at 2.6 GHz. Because each vCPU corresponds to an independent physical core with one thread per core, workloads avoid resource contention common to simultaneous multithreading environments. Cache resources comprise 64 KB L1 data cache and 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, alongside a shared 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 192.0 GB, maintaining an even 4.0 GB per core allocation. Local physical storage is directly integrated, supplying 2,850 GB of NVMe SSD instance capacity, paired with a baseline network speed of 22 Gbps. The instance does not include a GPU accelerator.

Synthetic and application benchmarks highlight strong multi-threaded compute and subsystem throughput. Multi-core testing delivers top-quartile results, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 73,480.11 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 19,368.0, with clang software compilation reaching 52,059.0. Memory subsystems perform exceptionally well, posting a top-decile PassMark memory score of 3,137.5 along with uncached large-block read speeds of 252.88 GB/sec and cached reads of 4,651.55 GB/sec. Application-oriented tests show strong results for caching and I/O-adjacent workloads, generating 76.17 million Redis SET operations per second and 66.05 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Conversely, single-core benchmarks reflect average scores, such as 1,532.89 in stress-ng and 1,534.0 in Geekbench.

The instance architecture presents a clear efficiency advantage for parallelized tasks through high core density and balanced memory per vCPU. Bundling 2,850 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage eliminates network latency overhead for scratch disks or transient data stores, providing cost efficiency advantages compared to attaching high-IOPS network volumes. However, the reliance on the arm64 architecture necessitates compatible software builds and excludes x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512. Given these characteristics, the instance is well suited for high-concurrency database engines, in-memory caching systems, large-scale build and CI/CD clusters, and data ingestion pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m7gd.12xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-based cloud server equipped with 48 dedicated physical arm64 cores powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processors clocked at 2.6 GHz. Operating without simultaneous multithreading, each core provides isolated execution backed by 192 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server bundles 2,850 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD instance storage and offers a 22 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating without discrete GPU hardware. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-core processing, exceptional memory bandwidth, and high database execution rates, including 76.17 million Redis SET operations per second and robust software compilation speeds. While single-threaded performance registers near the median, aggregate compute density and top-tier memory speeds yield high efficiency for resource-intensive applications. These technical capabilities make the m7gd.12xlarge an effective platform for distributed transactional databases, in-memory caching clusters, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and high-throughput web serving environments.
